title: Oil Prices Dip as Rising U.S. Inventories Deepen Oversupply Fears
summary: Oil prices eased in early Asian trading on Wednesday as traders reacted to another rise in U.S. oil inventories and signals continue to mount that global supply is running ahead of demand. At the time of writing, WTI was trading at $60.59 per barrel, down 0.25% on the session, while Brent slipped to $64.71, down by roughly 0.3%.
